answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to accumulate costly, verifiable work history before it can transact at scale, like a sparrow earning trust one delivery at a time rather than appearing fully formed. New identities start in a shallow dune of low limits, and only sustained, attested performance lets them cross the canyon to higher-value work. Spawning a thousand fakes gains nothing, because none has history, so an attacker must pay the full time-and-computation cost for every single one.
